creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A bundle can't carry the `post_install` step it depends on, so every profile that installs the bundle has to repeat the step, and a profile that forgets it installs a bundle that does nothing.

The auto-approval bundle does nothing until `render.rad` runs, so the same step sits in five places across three config repos: two profiles in one, a profile and a Codex post-install script in another, and a profile in the third. The bundle's description has to warn: "A profile that installs this must run auto-approval/render.rad in its post_install, or the policy only sits on disk." memri's install step is repeated per profile the same way.

Proposed: let a bundle (or an asset) declare `post_install` steps that run whenever it is in the resolved set, deduplicated across imports and run after files are written.

Things to decide while building it:

- Order: where bundle steps run relative to the profile's own steps, and to each other. Resolution order of the bundles is the natural default.
- Identity for deduplication: a bundle imported twice, through two paths, should run its step once. Keying on bundle plus step name probably works.
- Paths: a step's command will usually live in the bundle's own source, so it needs a way to name a file relative to that source (or to `TAI_TARGET_DIR`) that works whichever repo imports it.

This builds on card `run-post-install-as` (each step succeeds or fails on its own, with its own re-baseline), so do that one first. The approval-policy asset (card `add-an-approval`) would remove the auto-approval case, but memri's setup still needs this.

(Moved from GitHub issue #13, part 2.)
title: Let a bundle declare the post_install steps it depends on
